title: yamt
tagline: A three-way merge window like the one in JetBrains IDEs, for every git conflict at once. 🔀
why: PhpStorm's three-pane merge window is the only merge tool I find usable. VS Code's merge editor, its extensions and the TUI mergetools all felt unintuitive.

They all start from the `<<<<<<<` conflict markers. Once git has collapsed a merge into markers the base is gone, so you can see _that_ two sides differ but not _what each side changed_. yamt never parses a conflict marker: it reads the base, your side and theirs from git's index and diffs them itself.

`git mergetool` opens one file at a time, and real merges touch many files. yamt takes over the whole merge: every conflicted file in one window, your side on the left, theirs on the right, the result in the middle.

sections.title: Use
body: When `git merge`, `git rebase` or `git cherry-pick` stops with conflicts, run `yamt` in the repository (or `yamt --repo <path>` from anywhere). yamt starts from a terminal inside a repository; double-clicking it in a file manager or Finder shows nothing.
bullets: The file list on the left shows every conflicted file with git's view of it (resolved or not, also when you run `git add` elsewhere); click one to open it. Drag its edge to make it wider.
The right pane's header names what you are merging in: the branch, or the commit and its subject.

Each change has an arrow that applies it to the result and a × that ignores it; press one and drag up or down to apply or ignore several at once (one undo step). Ctrl+click (Cmd+click on macOS) a highlighted change applies it. The toolbar applies all non-conflicting changes from the left or from the right in one click.
The result pane is a normal editor: type, Tab / Shift+Tab indent and outdent, undo and redo. Ctrl+F (Cmd+F) finds text in whichever pane you clicked.

**Mark resolved** writes the result, stages the file and opens the next unresolved one. It turns blue once nothing is left to process. **Reset**, next to "Result", brings the conflict back as git left it.

A file deleted on one side and changed on the other shows the changed side with its changes, and two buttons: **Keep** and **Delete**. Other files the editor cannot show (binary, symlinks, submodules) get a choice between the two sides.
Closing the window exits with status 0 when every file is resolved and 1 otherwise, so scripts can tell. Then continue as usual (`git commit`, `git rebase --continue`, …).

sections.title: Make it feel built in
body: `git mergetool` is not the way to start yamt: it runs the tool once per file, while yamt handles all files in one window.

sections.title: Build from source
body: You need the Rust toolchain from `rust-toolchain.toml` (installed by [rustup](https://rustup.rs) on the first `cargo` call), [pnpm](https://pnpm.io), and on Linux webkit2gtk-4.1 (Arch: `webkit2gtk-4.1`; Debian/Ubuntu: `libwebkit2gtk-4.1-dev`).

sections.title: NVIDIA on Linux
sections.body: WebKitGTK's DMABUF renderer crashes on some NVIDIA setups. yamt switches it off by itself when the NVIDIA driver is loaded; a value you set for `WEBKIT_DISABLE_DMABUF_RENDERER` wins.
